findings.where: Nav bar lockup (arches mark + "MMM INFRA") and the large hero aqueduct mark, at both widths
findings.fault: The logo is shown in colours Mark does not hold. The arches use the tile's near-black 'cut' ink instead of the logo grey #404040. The wordmark is set in that same dark ink instead of the logo blue #0070C0, so the logo's only brand colour is gone. This was done to suit the granite ground: a ground that dark cannot hold the full-colour logo. The design changed the logo to fit the ground, when the ground should have been chosen to fit the logo.
findings.who_objects: Mark, the client. His mark is the one fixed part of the identity, and the brief says it stays. Here it appears as a one-colour dark version he never supplied or approved, and the brand blue that ties the site to his existing logo has disappeared. A version like this needs his yes before it is shown as the identity.

findings.where: Minium red across the page: the hero's two-line name and role heading, the article title, the motion sketch's 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED', the easing curve, the 'M' capital in the texture panel, and the 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: The direction promises one accent that leads to the action, but red is spread over large display areas. In the first screen the red headline is far bigger and heavier than the red button under it, so red no longer marks 'this is what to do'. The curve and the texture capital break the palette's own rule too: they are neither headings nor the action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development bank who scans the first screen for how to contact Mark: the headline takes the colour that should point them to the button. The layout and animation rounds would also object, because they inherit a red that has no single job.

findings.where: Palette strip, the fourth swatch labelled LIME
findings.fault: The Lime swatch is a second solid minium block with 'AA' on it. The four-swatch row therefore reads as red twice at equal size, and the actual lime colour shows only as two small letters.
findings.who_objects: Mark, comparing five directions by their palettes: at a glance this one looks like it has two reds, and its fourth colour is hard to see.
